title: Integral exceptional inverse image along the projective line and affine space
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$, and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$. Work with separated finite-type $k$-schemes and their $k$-morphisms, as in [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. For each such scheme $T$, use the bounded constructible category $\Dbc(T,\mathcal O_E)$ of [sk-def-sfb-constructible], in the unbounded derived category of modules over the pulled-back condensed coefficient sheaf $\mathcal O_{E,T}$. Put $\mathcal L(T)=\Loc(\Dbc(T,\mathcal O_E))$ as in [sk-def-localizing-closure]. Let $f^!$ be the right adjoint supplied by [det-prop-int-brown-adjoint]. Tate twists mean [sk-def-sp-tate-twist].

For a standing scheme $Y$ and $d\in\mathbb N$, let $q:\mathbf P^1_Y\to Y$ and $p_d:\mathbf A^d_Y\to Y$ be the structural projections ([def-nagata-projective-space-base-change], [def-sbc-affine-space]). Then:
1. $Rq_*\dashv q^*(1)[2]$ on $\mathcal L(\mathbf P^1_Y)$ and $\mathcal L(Y)$, and $q^!\simeq q^*(1)[2]$.
2. $p_d^!\simeq p_d^*(d)[2d]$ as functors $\mathcal L(Y)\to\mathcal L(\mathbf A^d_Y)$.
3. $q^*(1)[2]$ and $p_d^*(d)[2d]$ map $\Dbc(Y,\mathcal O_E)$ into $\Dbc(\mathbf P^1_Y,\mathcal O_E)$ and $\Dbc(\mathbf A^d_Y,\mathcal O_E)$ respectively.

proof.text: First check the candidate right adjoints are functors of the required categories. By [sk-def-sp-tate-twist], $\mathcal O_{E,T}(r)$ is pro-étale locally free of rank one for every integer $r$. Taking the single stratum $T$ and the local scalar module $\mathcal O_E$ in [sk-def-sfb-constructible] shows that this sheaf, in degree zero, belongs to $\Dbc(T,\mathcal O_E)$. Pullback and tensor preserve $\Dbc$ by [sk-lem-int-tensor]; shifts preserve boundedness and just reindex the cohomology sheaves in its definition. Thus $g^*(-)(r)[s]$ preserves $\Dbc$ for every standing morphism $g$ and integers $r,s$. The inverse image is exact by [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients], and its derived adjunction to $Rg_*$ is [def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull-adjunction]. It preserves small coproducts by [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits]. Tensoring with the invertible Tate sheaf is an exact equivalence with inverse the opposite twist, so it also preserves coproducts; shifts do too. Consequently the preimage under $g^*(-)(r)[s]$ of $\mathcal L$ is a localizing subcategory containing $\Dbc$, and hence contains $\mathcal L$ by [sk-def-localizing-closure]. This proves the typing of all candidate functors and already proves clause (3). For the integral coefficients used here, [det-def-localizing-closure-ctf-equals-bc](2) identifies $\Dctf=\Dbc$ and their localizing closures. It applies because every standing scheme is qcqs. Thus the notation agrees with [sk-def-localizing-closure], and all later uses of [sk-thm-sf-pf-adic] on $\Loc(\Dctf)$ are uses on precisely $\mathcal L$.

source.place: (3), with the localizing-category typing needed in (1) and (2)

proof.text:
Put $P=\mathbf P^1_Y$, $W=P\times_Y P$, and let $p_1,p_2:W\to P$ and $\Delta:P\to W$ be the projections and diagonal. The projection $q$ is proper by [lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-proper]; the same statement over $P$ applies to each $p_i$. The diagonal is closed since the projective-line projection is separated, and is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper](a). These are standing separated finite-type morphisms. For every proper morphism here, [det-prop-int-brown-construction] compares its chosen compactification with the identity-open compactification, giving a natural isomorphism $R(-)_!\simeq R(-)_*$ on the same integral localizing categories. We use these comparisons throughout; their stated compatibility with composition therefore gives $Rp_{i*}\Delta_*=\mathrm{id}$ and $Rq_*Rp_{1*}=Rq_*Rp_{2*}$. Write $R_T=\mathcal O_{E,T}$. The integral proper projection formula [det-thm-sf-pf-adic-projection], applied to $\Delta$ and $\Delta^*p_1^*M=M$, gives a natural isomorphism
$$a_M:p_1^*M\otimes^L\Delta_*R_P\xrightarrow{\sim}\Delta_*M.$$
The type of the diagonal class is given by [det-prop-diagonal-tower-limit](3), before extension of scalars. The maps $\delta:\Delta_*R_P\to R_W(1)[2]$ and $t_q:Rq_*R_P(1)[2]\to R_Y$ are supplied by [det-prop-diagonal-tower-coefficients] from [det-prop-diagonal-tower-trace]. Define $\eta_M:M\to q^*Rq_*M(1)[2]$ by
$$M=Rp_{2*}\Delta_*M\xrightarrow{Rp_{2*}a_M^{-1}}Rp_{2*}(p_1^*M\otimes^L\Delta_*R_P)\xrightarrow{Rp_{2*}(1\otimes\delta)}Rp_{2*}p_1^*M(1)[2]\xrightarrow{\sim}q^*Rq_*M(1)[2].$$
The last arrow is inverse proper base change [sk-thm-sf-pf-adic], followed by the twist passage (the twist is pulled back from $Y$). Define $\varepsilon_K:Rq_*q^*K(1)[2]\to K$ as the projection formula isomorphism to $K\otimes^LRq_*R_P(1)[2]$, followed by $1\otimes t_q$ and the unitor. The coefficient and twist identifications are those of [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients]. All maps are natural and lie in the full localizing categories by step 1, the integral projection formula and the integral compact-support construction. Here properness includes separatedness, whose definition is closedness of the diagonal [def-weil-proper-morphism]. For the closed immersion $\Delta$, [det-lem-formal-closed-support-sheaves](2) gives exactness of $\Delta_*$, so $R\Delta_*=\Delta_*$ in the projection and composition formulas. For the map calculations below write $u_f$ and $c_f$ for the unit and counit of $f^*\dashv Rf_*$, distinct from the proposed $\eta,\varepsilon$. Let $b_2:q^*Rq_*\to Rp_{2*}p_1^*$ be the base-change map and $b_1:q^*Rq_*\to Rp_{1*}p_2^*$ the map for the square with the projections interchanged. By the mate formula [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate],
$$b_{2,N}=Rp_{2*}(p_1^*c_{q,N})\circ u_{p_2,q^*Rq_*N},\qquad
c_{p_2,p_1^*N}\circ p_2^*b_{2,N}=p_1^*c_{q,N}.$$
The pullback-composition identifications in these expressions are induced by $qp_1=qp_2$. Interchanging the displayed indices gives the explicit formula $b_{1,N}=Rp_{1*}(p_2^*c_{q,N})\circ u_{p_1,q^*Rq_*N}$ and its mate equation $c_{p_1,p_2^*N}\circ p_1^*b_{1,N}=p_2^*c_{q,N}$. Write $\pi_{f,L,N}:L\otimes^LRf_*N\to Rf_*(f^*L\otimes^LN)$ for the canonical projection-formula map. Its transpose is $1_{f^*L}\otimes c_{f,N}$; thus $\pi_{f,L,N}=Rf_*(1\otimes c_{f,N})\circ u_{f,L\otimes Rf_*N}$. These formulas use the ambient adjunctions, so apply to every object of $\mathcal L$, not just bounded objects. Two identifications used throughout: pullbacks compose by [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback], so $\Delta^*p_1^*\simeq(p_1\Delta)^*=\mathrm{id}$ as used for $a_M$; and derived pullback is compatible with derived tensor products, $g^*(K\otimes^{\mathbf L}L)\simeq g^*K\otimes^{\mathbf L}g^*L$ naturally in $K,L$, by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] applied to the pro-étale ringed topoi with the coefficient isomorphism $\alpha_g$ of [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients]. The latter is the comparison inside the projection-formula transpose $1_{f^*L}\otimes c_{f,N}$ above, and it gives $g^*(K(r))\simeq(g^*K)(r)$ for the pullbacks of twisted objects in steps 4, 6 and 7.

proof.text:
Compute the first triangle, keeping the projection indices fixed. Put $T=R_P(1)[2]$ and $T_W=p_1^*T\simeq p_2^*T\simeq R_W(1)[2]$, both identifications by [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients] since $qp_1=qp_2$. Let
$$v_M=Rp_{2*}(1\otimes\delta)\circ Rp_{2*}a_M^{-1}:M\to Rp_{2*}(p_1^*M\otimes^LT_W).$$
Then $\eta_M=(b_{2,M}\otimes1_T)^{-1}v_M$, with the twist passage in step 2 understood. Reassociate $Rq_*Rp_{2*}=Rq_*Rp_{1*}$ using $qp_2=qp_1$. Expanding the projection-formula and mate maps of step 2 gives, on this common source,
$$\varepsilon_{Rq_*M}\circ Rq_*((b_{2,M}\otimes1_T)^{-1})
=Rq_*(1_M\otimes t_{p_1})\circ Rq_*\pi_{p_1,M,T_W}^{-1}.$$
Here is the check of that rearrangement: replace each $b_i$ by $Rp_{i*}(p_{3-i}^*c_q)u_{p_i}$ and each $\pi_f$ by $Rf_*(1\otimes c_f)u_f$. Move the units past the tensor and class maps by naturality. The adjacent unit and counit on a pulled-back factor cancel by $c_{f,f^*L}\circ f^*u_{f,L}=1$, and those on a direct-image factor cancel by $Rf_*c_{f,N}\circ u_{f,Rf_*N}=1$, for $f=q,p_1,p_2$. The surviving trace is $t_{p_1}\circ b_{1,T}=q^*t_q$, exactly [det-prop-diagonal-tower-coefficients](3) for base change along $q:P\to Y$. This proves the displayed equality; it is a computation with the ambient adjunctions [def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull-adjunction] and the mate formulas [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate], not an extra compatibility hypothesis.
Next use naturality of the projection formula [sk-thm-sf-pf-adic] on $\delta$. On $\Delta_*R_P$ it satisfies $Rp_{1*}a_M\circ\pi_{p_1,M,\Delta_*R_P}=1_M$, after $Rp_{1*}\Delta_*=\mathrm{id}$: indeed $p_1\Delta=1_P$, and the transpose of this composite is the counit of the composite pullback/direct-image adjunction. The composite counit formula is [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]; hence $\pi_{p_1,M,\Delta_*R_P}^{-1}\circ Rp_{1*}a_M^{-1}=1_M$. Consequently
$$\varepsilon_{Rq_*M}\circ Rq_*\eta_M
=Rq_*\bigl(1_M\otimes(t_{p_1}\circ Rp_{1*}\delta)\bigr)=1_{Rq_*M}.$$
The last equality is the first integration identity of [det-prop-diagonal-tower-trace](2), extended integrally by [det-prop-diagonal-tower-coefficients](1). Proper direct-image composition and all category restrictions are those of [det-prop-int-brown-construction].

source.place: (1), first triangle; expanded from the rational triangle proof without using its rational statement

proof.text:
For the second triangle put $G=q^*(-)(1)[2]$ and use the notation $T,T_W,v$ of step 3. On $W$, the equality $qp_1=qp_2$ and Cartesian Tate coefficients identify $p_1^*GK=p_2^*GK$, after the tensor comparison $p_i^*(q^*K\otimes^{\mathbf L}R_P(1)[2])\simeq p_i^*q^*K\otimes^{\mathbf L}p_i^*R_P(1)[2]$ of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. We now keep the factor $GK$ outside $Rp_{2*}$. Expanding $G\varepsilon_K$ by its definition in step 2 gives
$$G\varepsilon_K\circ(b_{2,GK}\otimes1_T)^{-1}
=(1_{GK}\otimes t_{p_2})\circ\pi_{p_2,GK,T_W}^{-1}.$$
To check this equality, substitute $b_{2,N}=Rp_{2*}(p_1^*c_{q,N})u_{p_2,q^*Rq_*N}$ and $\pi_{f,L,N}=Rf_*(1\otimes c_{f,N})u_{f,L\otimes Rf_*N}$. Naturality moves $q^*K$ past these maps. The mate equation $c_{p_2,p_1^*N}\circ p_2^*b_{2,N}=p_1^*c_{q,N}$ contracts the counit from the projection formula; the remaining $p_2$ unit and counit contract by $Rp_{2*}c_{p_2,N}\circ u_{p_2,Rp_{2*}N}=1$. The trace term is $q^*t_q=t_{p_2}\circ b_{2,T}$ by [det-prop-diagonal-tower-coefficients](3). This yields precisely the displayed right-hand side, with the original twist of $GK$ left on that factor.
Precompose by $v_{GK}$. Projection-formula naturality on $\delta$ [sk-thm-sf-pf-adic] rewrites $\pi_{p_2,GK,T_W}^{-1}v_{GK}$ as $1_{GK}\otimes Rp_{2*}\delta$: on the diagonal $p_2\Delta=1_P$, so $Rp_{2*}a_{GK}\circ\pi_{p_2,GK,\Delta_*R_P}=1_{GK}$ and therefore $\pi_{p_2,GK,\Delta_*R_P}^{-1}\circ Rp_{2*}a_{GK}^{-1}=1_{GK}$. This identification follows by transposing the two maps and using the composite counit formula [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]; both transposes are the counit for $\Delta^*p_2^*=1$. Thus
$$G\varepsilon_K\circ\eta_{GK}
=1_{GK}\otimes(t_{p_2}\circ Rp_{2*}\delta)=1_{GK}.$$
The scalar equality is the second integration identity of [det-prop-diagonal-tower-trace](2), extended to $\mathcal O_E$ by [det-prop-diagonal-tower-coefficients](1). The twist identifications use [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients]; any interchange of the two shifts $[2]$ has Koszul sign $(-1)^4=1$. All adjunction and mate maps are the ambient ones [def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull-adjunction], [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate], and reassociation of direct images is [det-prop-int-brown-construction].

proof.text: For $F=Rq_*$ and $G=q^*(-)(1)[2]$, the maps $h\mapsto G(h)\eta_M$ and $a\mapsto\varepsilon_KF(a)$ between $\operatorname{Hom}(FM,K)$ and $\operatorname{Hom}(M,GK)$ are inverse: naturality moves $h$ or $a$ past the unit or counit, and steps 3 and 4 reduce the two composites to $h$ and $a$. Hence $F\dashv G$. For proper $q$, $Rq_!=Rq_*$ by [det-prop-int-brown-construction]. The current [det-prop-int-brown-adjoint] supplies $q^!$ for the chosen-compactification functor on exactly these module-object localizing categories. Transport its Hom bijection along the natural comparison $Rq_!\simeq Rq_*$ from [det-prop-int-brown-construction]. Both $G$ and $q^!$ are now right adjoints to the same functor $Rq_*$. Apply [det-sp-unique-right-adjoint] to these adjunctions: the component $q^!K\to GK$ is the transpose of the transported Brown counit $Rq_*q^!K\to K$, and the inverse is the Brown transpose of the counit $Rq_*GK\to K$ constructed in step 2. This gives $q^!\simeq G$, with uniqueness understood as compatibility with these counits. This proves clause (1).

For any standing base $T$, let $j:\mathbf A^1_T\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^1_T$ be the standard affine chart. Its compactification of the affine-line projection $u=q_Tj$ is recorded in [def-amb-affine-trace-tower]. Check quasi-compactness directly in the standard affine-chart construction: over an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}B$ of $T$, the two projective charts have coordinates $t=x_1/x_0$ and $s=x_0/x_1$. The inverse images under $j$ of these charts are $\operatorname{Spec}B[t]$ and $\operatorname{Spec}B[s,s^{-1}]$, since $s=t^{-1}$ on their intersection. Both are affine and hence quasi-compact. These projective charts, for all affine base opens, cover $\mathbf P^1_T$, so $j$ is quasi-compact. Extension by zero preserves the integral localizing categories by [det-cor-int-compactness-ii-extension-zero]; pullback does so by step 1. The ambient adjunction $D(j_!)\dashv D(j^*)$ stated in [def-sfb-dc-open-lower-shriek-adjunction] therefore restricts to these full subcategories. By [det-prop-int-brown-construction], the compactification $(j,q_T)$ gives a natural comparison $Ru_!\simeq Rq_{T*}D(j_!)$ from the chosen functor of [det-prop-int-brown-adjoint]. Since $j_!$ is exact, we write $j_!$ for $D(j_!)$ here. Transporting along this comparison uses precisely the same left functor as the Brown adjunction. For $A\in\mathcal L(\mathbf A^1_T)$ and $K\in\mathcal L(T)$ the natural Hom bijections are the following: the first is this comparison followed by the adjunction of steps 2–5 for the base $T$, the second is the restricted open adjunction, and
$$\operatorname{Hom}(Ru_!A,K)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(j_!A,q_T^*K(1)[2])\cong\operatorname{Hom}(A,j^*q_T^*K(1)[2])=\operatorname{Hom}(A,u^*K(1)[2]).$$
The last identification follows by the pullback composition of [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback] and the Cartesian coefficient and twist identifications [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients], with $j^*(q_T^*K\otimes^{\mathbf L}R_{\mathbf P^1_T}(1))\simeq j^*q_T^*K\otimes^{\mathbf L}j^*R_{\mathbf P^1_T}(1)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. Equivalently this is [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]. Thus $Ru_!\dashv u^*(-)(1)[2]$, and [det-prop-int-brown-adjoint] and [det-sp-unique-right-adjoint] identify $u^!$ with that functor. This proves clause (2) for $d=1$ uniformly in the base.

source.place: (2), restriction to the standard affine chart

proof.text:
Induct on $d$ with the claim $Rp_{d!}\dashv p_d^*(-)(d)[2d]$. For $d=0$, $\mathbf A^0_Y=Y$, $p_0=\mathrm{id}$ and the twist and shift are zero. The identity compactification in [det-prop-int-brown-construction] compares $Rp_{0!}$ with the identity functor, so this is the identity adjunction of [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] transported along that comparison. Comparing it with the Brown adjunction by [det-sp-unique-right-adjoint] also proves $p_0^!\simeq\mathrm{id}=p_0^*(0)[0]$. For the successor write $X_d=\mathbf A^d_Y$, $u_d:\mathbf A^1_{X_d}\to X_d$ and $p_{d+1}=p_du_d$, using the coordinate tower [def-amb-affine-trace-tower]. The base $X_d$ remains a standing scheme. By [det-prop-int-brown-construction], $Rp_{d+1,!}\simeq Rp_{d!}Ru_{d!}$. Composing the induction adjunction and the line adjunction of step 6 by [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] gives right adjoint
$$u_d^*\bigl(p_d^*(-)(d)[2d]\bigr)(1)[2]=p_{d+1}^*(-)(d+1)[2d+2].$$
Here pullbacks compose by [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback], pullback of the twist is its twist on $X_{d+1}$ by [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients], after the tensor comparison $u_d^*(N\otimes^{\mathbf L}R_{X_d}(d))\simeq u_d^*N\otimes^{\mathbf L}u_d^*R_{X_d}(d)$ of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], and the tensor powers in [sk-def-sp-tate-twist] give $(d)+(1)=(d+1)$. Exact pullback commutes with shifts, and shifts add; every shift is even. All functors preserve the localizing categories by step 1. Finally the composition and compactification comparisons are compatible by [det-prop-int-brown-construction], so transport the displayed composite adjunction to the chosen $Rp_{d+1,!}$ used in [det-prop-int-brown-adjoint]. Compare its right adjoint with $p_{d+1}^!$ by [det-sp-unique-right-adjoint], using the counit-compatible isomorphism, exactly as in step 5. This proves clause (2) for every $d\geq0$; clause (3) was proved in step 1.
